name: John the Baptist
bio: John the Baptist preached repentance in the Judean wilderness, dressed in camel's hair and living on locusts and wild honey, fulfilling Isaiah's prophecy of a voice crying out to prepare the way of the Lord. Crowds came from Jerusalem and Judea to be baptized by him in the Jordan, confessing their sins; he sharply warned the Pharisees and Sadducees not to presume on their heritage from Abraham, and declared that one far mightier than himself would soon baptize with the Holy Spirit and fire. When Jesus came to be baptized, John objected that he was unworthy, but complied at Jesus's insistence; as Jesus came up from the water, the Spirit descended on him like a dove and a voice from heaven declared him God's beloved Son (Matthew 3:1-17). John's imprisonment, death, and further testimony about Jesus are told in detail in the chapters ahead. When John was imprisoned, Jesus moved from Nazareth to Capernaum and began his public preaching ministry (Matthew 4:12-17). Later, John's own disciples asked Jesus why they fasted while his did not; Jesus replied that his presence was cause for celebration, like a wedding, with fasting to come only after he was taken away (Matthew 9:14-17).
